StoneX Group Inc. Investigation Notice: SueWallSt Notifies Investors of Pending Investigation Into StoneX Group Inc. (SNEX)

PR Newswire

NEW YORK, Nov. 19, 2026

StoneX beat revenue estimates and posted record full-year results, but SNEX shares sold off when quarterly diluted EPS of $0.66 came in $0.15 short of consensus expectations. SueWallSt notifies investors of a pending investigation into on behalf of shareholders who lost money in the decline.

NEW YORK, Nov. 19, 2026 /PRNewswire/ -- A revenue beat did not stop the selling. StoneX Group Inc. (NASDAQ: SNEX) shares dropped in after-hours trading after the Company reported fiscal fourth-quarter diluted EPS of $0.66, $0.15 below the roughly $0.81 Wall Street expected. SNEX shareholders who lost money in that sell-off should act now: submit your SNEX loss details today, or contact Joseph E. Levi, Esq. via email at jlevi@SueWallSt.com  or by telephone at (888) SueWallSt.

The market looked past the top line. StoneX reported operating revenue above expectations and record full-year results in the same release. Shares moved on profitability instead. Diluted EPS slipped from $0.70 in the prior-year quarter to $0.66, net income fell approximately 2%, and expenses rose even as operating revenue climbed.

SueWallSt notifies investors of a pending investigation on behalf of StoneX investors to determine whether they may be entitled to recover losses under the federal securities laws. Shareholders who purchased SNEX before the fiscal fourth-quarter report and were hit by the decline are the focus of the investigation.

Investors who held SNEX through the after-hours drop are encouraged to request a free review of your StoneX losses  or call (888) SueWallSt.

WHY SUEWALLST : SueWallSt is powered by Levi & Korsinsky LLP. Levi & Korsinsky LLP has established itself as a nationally-recognized securities litigation firm that has secured billions of dollars for aggrieved shareholders and built a track record of winning high-stakes cases. The firm has extensive expertise representing investors in complex securities litigation and a team of over 70 employees to serve our clients. For seven years in a row, Levi & Korsinsky has ranked in ISS Securities Class Action Services' Top 50 Report as one of the top securities litigation firms in the United States.

Frequently Asked Questions About the SNEX Investigation

Q: How much did SNEX stock drop?  A: SNEX shares were falling roughly 25% by midday on November 19, 2026, after StoneX Group Inc. reported fiscal fourth-quarter diluted EPS of $0.66. Analyst consensus was roughly $0.81 to $0.88, a shortfall of at least $0.15 per share, or more than 18.5%. Investors who purchased SNEX shares and suffered losses may be eligible to seek compensation.

Q: Which statements are being investigated as potentially misleading?  A: The investigation concerns whether StoneX Group Inc.'s statements to investors about its quarterly profitability and financial performance were accurate and complete. The stock price declined after the Company reported fiscal fourth-quarter diluted EPS well below expectations.

Q: What do SNEX investors need to do right now?  A: Investors may gather brokerage records showing purchase dates, share quantities, and prices paid.  Submit your information for a no-cost, no-obligation evaluation of your potential recovery. data.title: Qumulo and Cisco Turn Storage and Network Into a Unified Ransomware Defense
data.description:
Qumulo and Cisco Turn Storage and Network Into a Unified Ransomware Defense

From detection to containment in seconds: storage-layer detection now triggers network-layer isolation, with no manual handoff between security and infrastructure teams.

Qumulo today announced an integrated ransomware defense solution that pairs Qumulo NeuralProtect with Cisco Hypershield and Cisco N9300 Series Smart Switches. NeuralProtect applies multi-layered, real-time detection across the file system and the network, working with Cisco N9300 Series Smart Switches to isolate ransomware limiting its ability to spread and disrupt business operations.

Ransomware was involved in 39% of breaches according to the Cost of a Data Breach Report 2026 from IBM. The average cost of a breach has risen to $4.99 million globally, reaching $11.5 million for U.S. organizations. AI-accelerated attacks can now reach unstructured production data within minutes, yet most defenses still react after the damage is done, with detection occurring days after the attack was launched, exposing organizations to financial and reputational loss. Entropy detection, backup, and behavioral monitoring all respond only after malicious writes have hit production data.

NeuralProtect closes that gap with real-time scanning of all file changes, including writes and modifications. It combines models for known ransomware, zero-day variants, and entropy-evasion attacks with the integrated Bitdefender malware engine. On detection, it contains the attack at the storage layer and signals Cisco Hypershield, which updates L4 microsegmentation policies across Cisco N9300 Series Smart Switches.

How it works: from detection to containment in seconds

  1. Inspect: NeuralProtect analyzes file content in real time as it is written or modified.
  2. Detect: AI/ML models identify known and zero-day ransomware and malware, with a false-positive rate below 0.01%.
  3. Contain: Qumulo leverages instant, point-in-time, cryptographically locked snapshots, in combination with optional defensive policies that revoke the attacker’s write permissions, block the offending session, take defensive snapshots, and quarantine affected data.
  4. Isolate: NeuralProtect notifies Cisco Hypershield, which can be configured to use the information collected by NeuralProtect and can push updated policies to Cisco N9300 Smart Switches to isolate the source from the network and limit contamination of other systems.
  5. Alert: High-fidelity threat details go to the customer’s SIEM for incident response.
  6. Recover: Teams restore from known-good snapshots with an explicit record of affected files, enabling targeted recovery instead of rebuilding an entire data set from backup, which can take days to weeks and may overwrite potentially good files.

“Ransomware wins when defenders are too slow. Most organizations still measure resilience by how quickly they can recover. We think the better question is why you should lose the data at all. NeuralProtect stops the attack where the data lives, and Cisco Hypershield and N9300 Smart Switches can assist in preventing the attack from growing. Together, storage and network can coordinate a defense in seconds,” said Brandon Whitelaw, senior vice president of product at Qumulo.

“By integrating Cisco Hypershield with our N9300 Smart Switches, we are embedding security policy enforcement directly into the data center fabric. With our complementary solutions, Qumulo NeuralProtect helps customers translate high-confidence ransomware detections into immediate, automated host isolation with N9300 Smart Switch—securing their data and infrastructure at scale without the need for additional appliances or performance bottlenecks,” said Murali Gandluru, SVP Data Center Networking at Cisco.

Key benefits for joint customers

  • Prevention, not just recovery: Attacks are designed to be stopped at the point of write, in real time, on live storage before encryption spreads to production data or backups.
  • Coordinated, automated response: Storage-layer detection triggers network-layer isolation with no manual handoff between teams.
  • Security without a performance penalty: N9300 Smart Switches, built on Cisco Silicon One and AMD Pensando DPUs, provides robust L4 network segmentation without central security appliances.
  • Fewer false alarms: Content-based inspection improves security alert accuracy, keeping false positives below 0.01%, a 100 to 200 times improvement over comparable entropy-based tools.
  • Works with existing investments: The solution complements Endpoint Detection and Response (EDR), Security Information and Event Management (SIEM), and backup tools rather than replacing them.

Proven at scale

The NeuralProtect detection engine ran billions of deep file inspections in 2025. It stopped more than 48,000 ransomware threats and intercepted more than 4,000 malware threats, and protected customers paid zero ransoms.

Availability

The integrated solution is available now through Qumulo, Cisco, and their channel partners.

Learn more

  • Blog: From Detection to Containment in Seconds
  • Qumulo NeuralProtect: qumulo.com/product/neural-protect

About Qumulo

Qumulo is the only seven-time Leader in the Gartner Magic Quadrant for Distributed File and Object Storage and the foremost provider of cloud data platforms. With exabytes under management and more than 1,000 production customers, Qumulo is trusted by Fortune 500 companies and global enterprises to manage, store, curate, and protect their data, unlocking new possibilities and driving innovation across diverse industries. For more information, visit www.qumulo.com.

data.title: Asian Equities Fall as Anthropic's Blockbuster IPO Fails to Staunch AI Stock Selloff
data.description:
By Ronnie Harui

Asian equities fell Friday morning as Anthropic's blockbuster initial public offering failed to staunch the selloff in artificial intelligence stocks.

"The central story was the paradox of a record-breaking AI-sector IPO failing to arrest a broader market selloff," Commerzbank Research analysts said in a report. "Rather than acting as a rising tide, the listing appeared to trigger rotation out of existing AI-related names as investors redeployed capital into the new issue," they said.

Anthropic, the maker of the Claude chatbot, raised about $81 billion in the largest IPO on record, ending the overnight session with a market capitalization of roughly $1.3 trillion.

Anthropic shares opened more than 30% above their $83 IPO price, though gains moderated during the session to finish up 17% at $97.17 in their market debut. The pullback "coincided with declines in other AI-related stocks amid concerns about how higher interest rates affect technology valuations," said Antonio Di Giacomo, senior market analyst at XS.com, in an email.

The SPDR Select Sector Technology exchange-traded fund, which tracks the tech industry group of the U.S.' S&P 500, entered bear-market territory on Thursday, closing 1.9% lower at $160.69, more than 20% below its October peak.

Across Asia, South Korea's Kospi slid 4.7%, with chip-making index heavyweights SK Hynix shedding 6.3% and Samsung Electronics losing 4.8%. Japan's Nikkei Stock Average slipped 4.7%, as AI proxy SoftBank Group fell 15.6%, memory chipmaker Kioxia Holdings dropped 12.6%, and Advantest, a manufacturer of automatic test equipment for the semiconductor industry, declined 12.3%. Australia's S&P/ASX 200 benchmark index was down 0.9%.

Short-dated Asian and U.S. government bonds rose in price terms Friday morning as the equity-markets' selloff bolstered safe-haven demand for sovereign debt.

Yields on Australia's two-year government bonds declined 4 basis points to 4.6150% and on New Zealand's two-year sovereign notes fell 2 basis points to 3.8740%. U.S. two-year Treasury yields edged 2 basis points lower to 4.7429%% following Thursday's Treasury yield declines. Bond yields move inversely to prices.

"Risk aversion intensified, driving demand for U.S. Treasurys," two strategists at OCBC Group Research said in a report. "Investors continued to unwind crowded positions and reassess the macro outlook as Anthropic's record IPO sharpened scrutiny of stretched AI valuations and financing risks," the strategists added.

data.title: CUPE education workers deliver overwhelming strike vote mandate, demand Ford government address crisis of funding and staffing in Ontario schools
data.description:
CUPE education workers deliver overwhelming strike vote mandate, demand Ford government address crisis of funding and staffing in Ontario schools

Education workers represented by the Canadian Union of Public Employees' (CUPE) Ontario School Board Council of Unions (OSBCU) have delivered an overwhelming province-wide strike vote mandate, delivering a strong message that workers are prepared to take strike action if necessary to win the funding, staffing and supports Ontario schools desperately need.

With 94.2% voting YES, with a total of 52,901 ballots cast, OSBCU members have demonstrated strong support for their bargaining committee and its demands for better staffing, job security, wages and benefits. The result reflects years of frustration among education workers who are witnessing firsthand the consequences of years of underfunding, understaffing and neglect in Ontario’s publicly funded schools.

“OSBCU education workers are telling this government that enough is enough. Our schools are in crisis, our members are stretched beyond their limits, and students are not getting the support they deserve,” said Joe Tigani, President of the OSBCU. “This incredible strike mandate shows that our members are ready to fight for better schools. This government must bring meaningful proposals to the bargaining table.”

The OSBCU represents education workers across Ontario, including educational assistants, early childhood educators, custodians, school secretaries, library workers, IT and maintenance staff, child and youth workers and many others who are essential to supporting students and keeping Ontario’s publicly funded schools running.

77.5% of the OSBCU's 68,239 members voted. This number represents even more members than voted in the historic 2022 OSBCU strike vote which defeated the Ford Government’s anti-union and unconstitutional Bill 28, legislation which invoked the “notwithstanding clause” and prompted an outcry from the labour movement across Canada. The scale of OSBCU’s membership has grown significantly in recent years, revealing just how little the Ford Government is investing in stable, permanent jobs in education, forcing Ontario school boards to rely more and more on casual and temporary employment. New membership data, compiled using employee lists provided by school boards, shows that upwards of 20,000 OSBCU members are casual or temporary employees, far exceeding the number of casual members in previous years.

While the number of permanent education workers has remained relatively stagnant, school boards have increasingly relied on casual and temporary workers to fill staffing gaps. Some employees classified as casual work virtually full-time hours, while others are called in irregularly, often having to juggle multiple jobs to make ends meet. This growing reliance on precarious employment is another symptom of a system that desperately needs more permanent, stable positions.

OSBCU will meet with the provincial government and school board representatives on November 30 to table its bargaining proposals. The OSBCU is entering negotiations with solutions to the challenges facing Ontario schools, with funding and staffing at the centre of its priorities.

“We have the answers. We know what our schools need because our members are the people who keep them running every day. We are fighting for more staff, safer schools, better jobs and the resources students need to succeed,” Tigani said. “We’re calling on the Ford government to increase funding to public education and provide the education worker staff that our students and school communities deserve instead of forcing a disruption on the 2027 school year. This is about the future of publicly funded education in Ontario, and we are ready to fight for what our schools deserve.”

data.title: China Keeps Benchmark Lending Rates Unchanged
data.description:
China kept its benchmark lending rates unchanged Friday, as it has for more than a year, as narrowing net interest margins deterred lenders from trimming borrowing costs despite weak credit demand.

The one-year loan prime rate was held steady at 3.0% and the five-year rate was unchanged at 3.5%, said the People's Bank of China. Both rates have remained at these levels since May 2025.

The LPRs are calculated each month based on submissions from 20 major commercial banks in China. The rates serve as the benchmark for most new and existing corporate and household loans in China.

FRVO CLASS ACTION NOTICE: Glancy Prongay Wolke & Rotter LLP Files Securities Fraud Lawsuit On Behalf Of Fervo Energy Company (FRVO) Investors

Lawsuit asserts claims on behalf of investors who acquired Fervo Energy Company securities on date of IPO, May 13, 2026; lead plaintiff motions are due within 60 days of this notice.

Glancy Prongay Wolke & Rotter LLP ("Glancy") announces that it has filed a class action lawsuit in the U.S. District Court for the Southern District of Texas, captioned Nikolov v. Fervo Energy Company, Case No. 4:26-cv-10141, on behalf of persons and entities that purchased or otherwise acquired Fervo Energy Company ("Fervo" or the "Company") (NASDAQ: FRVO) Class A common stock pursuant and/or traceable to the registration statement and prospectus (collectively, the “Registration Statement”) issued in connection with the Company’s May 13, 2026 initial public offering (“IPO” or the “Offering”). Plaintiff pursues claims under Section 11 and 15 of the Securities Act of 1933 (the "Securities Act").

Investors are hereby notified that they have 60 days from the date of this notice to move the Court to serve as lead plaintiff in this action.

If you suffered a loss on your Fervo Energy Company investments, inquire about the Fervo Energy Company class action to learn about potentially pursuing claims to recover your loss under the federal securities laws.

Key details of the Fervo Energy Company case

  • Court: U.S. District Court for the Southern District of Texas
  • Case No.: 4:26-cv-10141
  • Class period: May 2026 IPO
  • Claims: Section 11 and 15 of the Securities Act
  • Lead plaintiff motions: due within 60 days from the date of this notice

What happened?

On October 6, 2026, during market hours, Morpheus Research published a report alleging that "Fervo has failed to disclose existential issues related to inconsistent production temperatures and premature thermal decline, excessive water loss, seismicity-related equipment damage, transmission capacity, and ballooning costs. In some cases, Fervo appears to have presented altered data and made material misstatements to investors, including in its [initial public offering] registration statement filed with the [United States Securities and Exchange Commission].”

By the commencement of this action, the Company’s stock price had closed as low as $7.79 per share, a more than 71% decline from the $27 per share IPO price.

What is the Fervo Energy Company lawsuit about?

The complaint filed in this class action alleges that throughout the Class Period, Defendants made materially false and/or misleading statements, as well as failed to disclose material adverse facts about the Company's business, operations, and prospects. Specifically, Defendants failed to disclose to investors that: (1) that Fervo’s pilot plant was experiencing inconsistent production temperatures and premature thermal decline; (2) that Fervo’s EGS operations were experiencing significant injected water loss at a level above the rate the Company’s commercial plans required; (3) that Fervo’s drilling costs were not declining as represented, including as misleadingly represented given previously published data; (4) that Fervo lacked sufficient transmission capacity to deliver power to its California customers as planned, including the transmission path underlying the Company’s approximately 290 MW of rights which was scheduled for retirement before Cape Station Phase II’s targeted 2028 COD; and (5) as a result, Defendants' positive statements about the Company's business, operations, and prospects were materially misleading and/or lacked a reasonable basis at all relevant times.

If you purchased or otherwise acquired Fervo Energy Company securities during the Class Period, you may move the Court no later than 60 days from the date of this notice to ask the Court to appoint you as lead plaintiff.

Contact us to participate or learn more

If you wish to learn more about this action, or if you have any questions concerning this announcement or your rights or interests with respect to these matters, please contact Glancy about the Fervo Energy Company lawsuit, email shareholders@glancylaw.com, or call 310-201-9150 (toll-free: 888-773-9224).

If you inquire by email, please include your mailing address, telephone number, and number of shares purchased.

To be a member of the Class you need not take any action at this time; you may retain counsel of your choice or take no action and remain an absent member of the Class. No class has been certified yet in the Fervo Energy Company case.

Frequently Asked Questions

Who is eligible? Persons and entities that purchased or otherwise acquired Fervo Energy Company securities on May 13, 2026 and suffered losses may be members of the proposed class in the Fervo Energy Company securities lawsuit.

What is the Fervo Energy Company lead plaintiff deadline? Motions to serve as lead plaintiff in the Fervo Energy Company class action must be filed within 60 days from the date of this notice.

What is a lead plaintiff? In the Fervo Energy Company class action, the lead plaintiff is the investor, or group of investors, that the court appoints to represent all class members and oversee the case. Under the Private Securities Litigation Reform Act, courts generally presume the movant with the largest financial interest is the most adequate lead plaintiff.

Does it cost anything to contact Glancy or participate in this action? Glancy represents Fervo Energy Company investors on a contingency fee basis, so investors pay no attorneys' fees out of pocket. Any attorneys' fees and litigation expenses are paid only from a recovery, if one is obtained, and are subject to court approval.

data.title: My wife is bankrolling her family's trips to New York and it's draining our savings. Should I ask her to stop?
data.description:
By Quentin Fottrell

'Hotel rooms can cost as much as $400 per night'

"I feel that some of her family members have come to take advantage of that generosity." (Photo subject is a model.)

Dear Quentin,

My wife and I have a wonderful marriage, but there is one recurring issue that has become a significant source of frustration for me. While my wife is an exceptionally generous and giving person, I feel that some of her family members have come to take advantage of that generosity.

Several of her relatives regularly want to visit us in New York, traveling from Argentina. Given the long journey, these visits typically last around two weeks. Some of her nieces, nephews and siblings expect to visit every year.

The problem is that we live in a Manhattan apartment with limited space, and hosting guests for extended periods is a significant imposition on our daily routines, privacy and overall quality of life. Now that we also have a baby, the logistical and personal challenges are even greater.

My wife is extremely devoted to her family and, for whatever reason, seems to have difficulty saying no to their requests. I've gently raised my concerns several times, explaining that we simply don't have the space to accommodate so many guests.

Many of her relatives have limited financial means, so my wife often ends up covering not only their flights and accommodations, but also airport transportation, meals, entertainment and other expenses.

Don't miss: My older brother, who has no children, cut our only sister out of his will. I'll get everything instead. Do I tell her?

Space constraints

While I appreciate that this addresses some of the space constraints, it creates a separate issue: the considerable financial burden. Hotel rooms can cost as much as $400 per night, and the total cost of these visits can easily run into several thousand dollars.

Although my wife has her own money, these expenditures still have meaningful opportunity costs for our family. We have substantial financial priorities, including the high cost of childcare in New York City, saving toward purchasing a home and planning for our son's education.

It's also worth noting that we already travel to Argentina every year to visit her family. So it's not as though declining to host relatives in New York would prevent us from maintaining close relationships with them or spending time together.

I love my wife and I genuinely admire her generosity and commitment to her family. However, I'm increasingly feeling that her relatives' expectations are being prioritized over my comfort in our own home, our privacy and our family's financial goals.

I'm concerned that if this continues, my frustration will turn into resentment and undermine what is otherwise an excellent marriage. How can I establish reasonable boundaries? I don't want my wife to feel that I'm asking her to choose between me and her family.

The Husband

You can email The Moneyist with any financial and ethical questions at qfottrell@marketwatch.com. The Moneyist regrets he cannot reply to questions individually.

Related: 'It leaves me with a sour taste': My elderly mother gave our cousin $800 for a car repair. Should I be worried?

She could be afraid of angering or disappointing her relatives, issues that might be rooted in her upbringing and culture.

Dear Husband,

When words fail to change bad habits, enlist a pen and paper.

This is a domestic as well as a financial problem. Your wife is spending money in isolation and without keeping your overall financial goals in mind. You probably are too, perhaps in smaller ways. This bad habit, which only appears to be getting worse, needs to be broken.

The only way to accomplish this is to show her how much money these trips are costing your family, in real terms, as you also pay for childcare and rent, save for emergencies and your child's schooling and college education, and put money aside to buy a home.

Of course, making it personal will only get you both mired in hurt feelings and defensiveness, so you need to take her family out of the equation as much as possible and revisit your marriage vows - your pact to respect and honor each other.

You can have these conversations alone, or with the help of a financial adviser or counselor. I suggest the latter. A mediator can help you articulate your concerns, frame your questions as "I feel ..." rather than "You are ..." and prevent you from hurting each other's feelings.

Ultimately, you need to formulate a family policy rather than take potshots at your wife's family. You have reached a stage in your married life when you are working toward tangible financial goals, and spending thousands of dollars on third parties compromises that.

A financial therapist could help to field your concerns.

Emphasize your shared responsibility and the importance of working as a team. Hosting relatives every year impinges on your privacy and ability to relax in your own home, disrupts your daily routines and makes your responsibilities as new parents more challenging.

Eventually, your wife will have to find the words to say no to people, her family included. It's not always easy, but after you do it once, it gets easier. Given that she has set an unhealthy precedent, this conversation can start with a soft no - and the truth.

She can tell her family: "This year is impossible for us to host. We no longer have room. We have a young child and a lot of family and work commitments." For what it's worth, there's also a difference between relatives visiting your city and crashing at your place.

I feel confident that facing up to the reality of your financial situation will encourage your wife to stop spending money meant for your little family on visiting relatives. Hotels, theater tickets and meals all add up, and something is wrong if her family members all expect the royal treatment.

Any expenditure over $1,000 should have veto power.

Facing that reality means making big decisions together - and spending thousands of dollars a year on visiting relatives is categorically a big decision, even if it seems like it's actually lots of small acts of generosity. Any expenditure over $1,000 should be discussed and agreed upon.

Many couples have a "mutual veto" on a large purchase. Some have a dollar cap, the size of which depends on their income. Unless there are two yes votes, the veto kicks in. But a dollar cap of $1,000 doesn't mean you can spend $999 each on a bunch of relatives.

Finally, many couples have "yours, mine and ours" accounts. They have a joint account for shared bills, savings and vacation money, and smaller personal checking accounts for guilt-free "mad money" splurges. But everything is accounted for in the family ledger.

At the root of this problem is why your wife feels obliged to host her relatives. Our relationship with money is emotional and, although we probably don't like to acknowledge it, less logical than we might imagine. She could be afraid of angering or disappointing her family.

A financial therapist could help explore why your wife feels such a strong sense of familial duty, which may be rooted in her upbringing and culture. She may even feel guilty about having achieved a more financially comfortable life than her relatives.

Whatever the reason behind it, the open-house era of hosting relatives should come to a close.

data.title: CCTV4：Documentary 'OUR HOME, OUR YANGTZE' to Premiere Soon
data.description:
CCTV4：Documentary 'OUR HOME, OUR YANGTZE' to Premiere Soon

CCTV4：Documentary 'OUR HOME, OUR YANGTZE' to Premiere Soon

PR Newswire

BEIJING, Nov. 19, 2026

BEIJING, Nov. 19, 2026 /PRNewswire/ -- Across four episodes, Our Home, Our Yangtze tells a decade of change along the Yangtze River Economic Belt through four unusual narrators: a fish, a single kilowatt-hour of electricity, a microchip and a shipping container. Their stories explore ecological conservation, industrial upgrading, innovation-led growth and greater openness.

A fish swims through clear waters and past green banks, witnessing the patience and rewards of conservation. A kilowatt-hour passes through factories and cities, revealing the pulse of industrial renewal. A microchip travels from laboratory to production line, recording the build-up and breakthroughs of innovation. A shipping container crosses ports and sea routes, charting an ever-wider world of trade.

Each episode stands alone yet echoes the others. Through life, energy, intelligence and the movement of goods, the series reflects the changing Yangtze River Economic Belt.

Blending documentary realism with poetic expression, the series finds the epic in the everyday, allowing a decade of transformation to unfold through a migration, a light switched on, a calculation and a departure.

Avnet Declares Regular Quarterly Dividend

Avnet, Inc. (Nasdaq: AVT), a leading global technology distributor and solutions provider, announced that its Board of Directors has approved a regular quarterly cash dividend of $0.37 per share. The dividend will be paid on December 16, 2026, to shareholders of record as of the close of business on December 2, 2026.

As a leading global technology distributor and solutions provider, Avnet has served customers’ evolving needs for more than a century. Through regional and specialized businesses around the world, we support customers and suppliers at every stage of the product lifecycle. We help companies adapt to change and accelerate the design and supply stages of product development. With a unique viewpoint from the center of the technology supply chain, Avnet is a trusted partner that solves complex design and supply chain issues so customers can realize revenue faster.
